what: ANIMATION [the town's activities] (rule 218(a), Paolo 10/26, LOCKED: 'everyone on your company... you can see them in the settlement, maybe flirting with a girl, maybe drinking some beer, maybe walking around, maybe talking to people... make it feel alive'). THE KEPT SOURCE OF EVERY TOWN ACTIVITY (rule 128): six things a man of his company does in a town, each a loop of held keys on the rig's man (the skeleton every person in the game is built on, so one list fits every look), with its own breaths and a few variants, so no two men do it in step. The pose ops, the axes and the bones are the idles' (records/target/animation/BOHEMIA_EVERYBODY_IDLES.json, read by the tool: a part named here that is not in this file's parts is the idles' part of that name). Walking the street is the walk every man already has (slices/rig_walk, RUN TWO's sheet: 'walk_plain'), steered by the player's wander (engine/bohemia_idles.js), its stops played as 'stall' or the bare idles. AND, rule 245 (Paolo 10/26: 'a live show... of your characters looting the bodies and walking between them... research what people typically do after battles'), THE MINUTES AFTER A FIGHT: four acts of the set 'after' (an activity's 'set'; a town act has none), researched and cited in records/BOHEMIA_ANIMATION_THE_MINUTES_AFTER_A_FIGHT_RESEARCH_10_26_26.md: LOOT, TEND, BIND, BREATH, on the same grammar with two ops more, the holds' own: ['KNEEL', side, front, seat] (one knee down, the pelvis dropped by the skeleton's own lengths) and ['REACH', side, from, [f, u, l], pole] (the hand carried to a point by the arm's two bones; from a joint, 'G' the floor under his pelvis, or 'mid_LF' halfway along his left forearm), and a 'limb' prop wound round a bone (the bandage). AND, rule 259 (Paolo 10/26: 'if I enter camp mode and time is passing I should see my character and my whole team... healing... repairing their armour... helping other members if they're healthy'), THE CAMP'S ACTS: the set 'camp' (LIE hurt and bandaged, SLEEP on his bedroll, MEND a cut sitting by the fire, REPAIR the car door with a hammer and tape, COOK at the pot, CLEAN his rifle, RISE once when healed), one op more: ['LIE', back, roll, height] (the pose as he would hold it standing, tipped back about his pelvis, rolled about his facing, let down to the floor; no plant).
keys: three a beat at 120; a pose is HELD (Crashbox stop-motion, rule 115(d)), never blended; a slot is two bars (24 keys) and starts and ends on the activity's REST pose, so any slot of an activity follows any other. AN ENVELOPE RAMPS SLOWER THAN THE GRID: a pose held ONE key sits between two different poses on the way (never a flicker out and back), the two sides of a turn never touch, and the gate measures every joint's travel between two drawn keys on the posed model itself (records/target/animation/towns/<look>/joints.json).

bottle.what: a green beer bottle, 23 cm, a big paper label gone pale and a bottle cap, held in his fist by its body, the neck up out of the thumb side (green glass and a pale label: a brown bottle was lost on a brown coat, measured on the first preview)

can.what: a tin of food off the stall, its paper label red and rust at the rims

cigarette.what: the idles' hand-rolled cigarette, the same 7 cm and ember (the bare set's smoke)

smoke.what: the idles' three grey puffs, the breath he lets out

seat.what: the work's slatted crate, a third taller, set on end behind his heels: what he sits on (a stoop, a crate, a step: the town's own props stand where RUN THREE puts him)

battery.what: a battery out of the dead man's pocket (BATTERIES ARE THE MONEY, Paolo 9/4): a fat cell, 10 cm, a dark wrap and a bright copper cap so it reads at 57 px a metre, held across his fist

bandage.what: a strip of dirty cloth wound round his left forearm, a brown stain through it: the cut he binds (TCCC's field dressing in a ruin's rags)

wrap.what: a wide strip of dirty cloth round his belly, a brown stain through it: the badly hurt man's dressing

bedroll.what: his bedroll on the ground under him, olive canvas with a rolled end under his head

door.what: the car door he is mending, laid flat before him, COOK's faded teal, its window a dark hole

hammer.what: a claw hammer, its wooden handle in his fist, the steel head up out of the thumb side

pot.what: a black iron pot over the fire (the fire is the camp's), something brown in it

spoon.what: a long wooden spoon, its bowl down in the pot

rifle.what: his rifle across his knees, held at the fore-end in his left fist: a worn wooden stock, the action and the barrel (a stand-in in his gang's long gun's shape)

rag.what: an oily rag bunched in his fist

bundle.what: a rolled bundle out of the cart (a tarp or a bedroll tied in two places) held across both fists: the tool aims it from his right fist to his left on every key

stake.what: a tent stake driven in before him, pale split wood, a guy line off its head running away to the tent (CAMP TWO's)

kindling.what: the fire laid and not yet lit: a ring of stones, dry grass, a tepee of sticks over it

flame.what: the flame catching in the grass: orange low, yellow at its tip

lighter.what: a red plastic lighter in his fist

drink.what: DRINKING A BEER at a bar or a stall: the bottle at his belt, a sip, a long swig with the head back, a look round, the bottle never put down

smoke.what: SMOKING: the cigarette held low between drags, a drag and the smoke let out, a hip out with a hand on it

talk.what: TALKING WITH SOMEONE: two people, turns. While he has the word he talks with his hands (an open hand, both hands, a point, a chop); while the other has it he listens (nods, a tilt of the head, hands on his hips, a laugh). The partner plays the same clock half a turn on, so one talks while the other listens

turns.why: his turn and the other's, a slot each: the partner's clock is one slot on, so the two never talk at once

flirt.what: FLIRTING: his weight on one leg, the head tipped, leaning in to her, a laugh, a hand to the back of his neck; beside a wall a hand up on it (o.wall: only where RUN THREE stands him with a wall at his right hand)

sit.what: SITTING on a crate (a step, a stoop): his hands on his knees, his elbows on them leaning forward, leaning back on his hands, a look round

stall.what: LOOKING AT A STALL: bent a little over the goods, looking along them, a hand out to pick a tin up, turning it over, putting it back

loot.what: LOOTING THE DEAD (FM 3-21.8's search of the dead; Sledge, Juenger, Waterloo): down on his right knee by the body before him (RUN FOUR lays him at a body, facing it), his hands in its coat, a battery pulled out, held up and looked at, pocketed at his hip, a glance over his shoulder, both hands back in

tend.what: KNEELING BY A WOUNDED FRIEND (TCCC's tactical field care: pressure on the wound, talking to him): down on a knee by him lying before him, both hands pressing on him, leaning in to talk, a hand to his head, a look round for help, a nod

bind.what: BINDING A CUT (TCCC's field dressing): down on a knee, his left forearm across him, the strip wound over and under it with his right hand, the end pulled tight in his teeth, the hand tried

breath.what: CATCHING HIS BREATH (Grossman, On Combat: the backlash after the adrenaline): standing bent over with his hands on his knees, heaving, up with his hands on his hips and his head back, his own hands held before him shaking, the forearm across his face, a look round

lie.what: LYING HURT (rule 259(a): badly hurt, low hit points or a fresh injury): on his back, a bloody wrap round his belly, his hand pressed on it, his other arm on the ground, the knee drawn up; breathing, the head turning, a wince with both knees up. A friend kneels by him with 'tend' (the minutes after a fight's), facing him

sleep.what: SLEEPING (rule 259(a): at night): on his back on his bedroll, his hands on his belly, a knee up, his head tipped, slow breaths, now and then the head to the other side or the other knee

mend.what: BINDING A CUT BY THE FIRE (rule 259(a): hurt): sitting on a crate, his left forearm across him, a strip wound over and under it, the end pulled in his teeth, the arm tried (the bind's arms on the sit's legs)

repair.what: MENDING HIS ARMOUR (rule 259(a): armour broken): down on a knee at a car door laid flat before him, his left hand holding its edge, a claw hammer in his right, beating it on the beat; tape run round with both hands; a look at the work

cook.what: COOKING (rule 259(a): healthy): down on a knee by the fire, stirring the pot on it with a long wooden spoon, round and round, a taste off the spoon, a look round

clean.what: CLEANING HIS GUN (rule 259(a): healthy): sitting on a crate, his rifle across his knees in his left fist, an oily rag run up and down the barrel, a look round

rise.what: GETTING UP, HEALED (rule 259(a): 'a man who heals gets up and joins the others'): ONE SLOT (24 keys, two bars) from lying on his back to standing: tipping up to sit, onto a knee, up. CAMP plays it once (o.since the moment he heals) and then his next act; its rest is the standing he ends on

unpack.what: UNPACKING THE CART (rule 269(c): they pitch the camp): standing at the cart before him, his hands on its rim, bent into it rummaging, a rolled bundle hauled up to his chest and tossed to his left onto the pile, back to the rim

stake.what: DRIVING A TENT STAKE (rule 269(c)): down on a knee, his left fist round the stake, the claw hammer up and down on its head on the beat; the back of his fist across his brow; a look up the line to the tent

light.what: LIGHTING THE FIRE (rule 269(c)): down on a knee at the laid fire, a lighter flicked in his cupped hands, the flame catching in the grass; bent low blowing on it; it dies, again; back up with a hand on his knee, a look round

timelines.why: every slot is 24 keys (two bars at 120) and ends on its activity's rest pose; a one-key hold is a step on the way, never a flicker

never_adjacent.why: the two sides of a turn never touch in one drawn key (his 'tweaking', 9/21)
